paper.title: TeleEgo: Benchmarking Egocentric AI Assistants in the Wild

evidence.paraphrase: Synchronized first-person video, ambient audio/dialogue, and manually verified speech transcripts plus visual narrations from five participants over three consecutive days (>14 h per participant), all aligned to a single global timeline across work/study, lifestyle, social, and outing domains.

12 subtasks grouped into Memory (recalling past events, from short-term object state to hour-scale sequences), Understanding (current-moment semantics, causality, intent), and Cross-Memory Reasoning (linking temporally distant events into narrative structure); 3,291 human-verified QA items in single-choice, binary, multiple-choice, and open-ended formats.

Models are evaluated under a strictly streaming protocol. Real-Time Accuracy scores correctness within a 5 s decision window, and Memory Persistence Time measures how long an item remains correctly retrievable after it was first answered correctly, without replaying the evidence - a direct measure of persistent retention over a multimodal stream.

adjudication_notes: primary_modality set to video_streaming: the central persistent experience is a continuous egocentric video stream evaluated online; audio/speech and text narration are synchronized secondary channels.
No architecture record created: TeleEgo evaluates existing multimodal models under a streaming protocol and does not propose its own memory architecture.
